chapter: Booker T, the brass bands and the Pelican band
title: Trying to name the Pelican band drummer, Cook Shop Son
summary: Dawson cannot recall the drummer's name, an uptown man; Allen suggests drummers, and Dawson finally recalls the nickname Cook Shop Son because his mother kept a cook shop on Liberty Street.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: And who did you say the drummer was?
Uh, I don't know if he didn't even, uh, uh.
Well, who did he play with?
He, he, uh, all I knew him, he never did play with no other band, but he, he was a good little drummer. He's from uptown.
Uh. Not, well let me name some drummer, see if you know him. D.D. Channel was from uptown, huh? No. Mac Murray? No. Uh, Willigans? No. Wasn't that guy named Tillman?
Uh. You're kind of running out of uptown drummer from uptown. Uh, hmm.

Now there was one drummer that, that, that he used it most of the time. I think it was, he used this drummer more than he did any of them. The one, they had a boy they called Cook Shop Son.

He was, uh, he was the first drummer played with, uh, Edward Clinton. Yeah, his mama had a cook shop. His mama had a cook shop on, on, was it Frank, Liberty Street, Max Liberty, Saratoga. By Rischak? But every time we needed him we had to go by the cook shop and get him in.
